title: The Hungry Hymn
premise: Isandro Lockridge returns to the decaying village of Vesper's Hollow to bury his twin brother Anselm, only to learn the body in the coffin is not Anselm at all. A bell that was melted down in 1911 begins to ring at dusk, calling villagers to a founding ritual that was never finished, one that feeds memory to the land in exchange for the town's survival. Isandro, who has spent his life hiding behind his brother's identity, discovers he is the ritual's intended final signer. In the climax, he completes the founders' rite but rewrites its terms, offering his own remembered childhood instead of the village's souls, and the bell falls silent as the last resident signs the papers, leaving Isandro to bury his brother a second time and finally claim his own name.
about_author: Marguerite Galloway is the pen name of a former church archivist who spent a decade cataloguing rural parish records across the American interior, where she collected the hymnals, ledgers, and burial disputes that seed her fiction. She writes horror that treats bureaucracy and belief as equally haunted, and she still cannot hear a bell without counting the strokes.

chapters.title: The Wrong Body
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He arrives in Vesper's Hollow to arrange his twin Anselm's funeral and discovers the corpse's hands bear none of Anselm's scars. The undertaker, a found-family figure named Odile, quietly agrees to delay the burial. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in grief, and the first crack in Isandro's careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Settling into the brothers' childhood house, he catalogs its doors each night, a ritual of control. He finds Anselm's journal, half-burned, referencing a hymn 'that must be sung to the end.' Emotional beat: the comfort of compulsive routine curdling as the house seems to add a door that wasn't there before.

chapters.title: A Ringing That Should Not Be
chapters.summary: Isandro and Odile's shared POV. At dusk the church bell rings, though the parish record and a scorched beam confirm it was melted down in 1911. Villagers stop in the street, faces slack, then continue on as if nothing happened. Emotional beat: vertigo, the horror of a shared delusion no one will admit to sharing.

chapters.title: The Founders' Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. In the church archive, Odile shows Isandro the founders' ledger: a covenant binding the village's collective memory to the land, renewed by a signature every generation. The last living signer is dying, and the papers await a new name. Emotional beat: the lure of belonging versus the corruption of what belonging costs.

chapters.title: What the Land Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Villagers begin forgetting things, names, recipes, their dead, and Isandro starts remembering events that never happened to him: Anselm's memories, bleeding across the twin bond. Emotional beat: identity dissolving, the terror of inheriting a life that was never yours.

chapters.title: The Hymn in the Walls
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. He traces the humming in the house to a sealed room where the founders rehearsed the Hungry Hymn, the unfinished final verse of the covenant. Anselm's journal reveals he came home to finish the ritual and failed. Emotional beat: grief reframed as betrayal; his brother chose the village over him.

chapters.title: Signers and the Signed
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The last signer, old Mother Casque, summons them and confesses the covenant's true price: each renewal erases one villager entirely from every memory but the land's. She offers Isandro the pen. Emotional beat: temptation, power offered as rescue, its corruption visible in her hollowed eyes.

chapters.title: Anselm, Singing
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The bell rings at midnight and Anselm appears, or the land wearing him, leading villagers in the Hymn toward the church. Isandro must decide whether the figure is his brother resurrected or a lure. Emotional beat: longing weaponized; found family versus the family that fed on him.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, climax. In the church, he seizes the pen and signs, but speaks his own name, Isandro, and sings the final verse rewritten: he offers his hoarded memories of childhood, his hiding, his grief, as payment instead of the villagers. The bell cracks mid-stroke. Emotional beat: self-annihilation chosen freely, power refused.

chapters.title: Buried Twice, Named Once
chapters.summary: Isandro and Odile's shared POV. The village wakes remembering everything, including Isandro, who has lost his earliest years and must rebuild himself from Odile's found-family care. They bury the body a second time, under his brother's true name, and the papers close with the covenant ended. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace; memory surrendered, identity kept.
